title: What training do Victorian security guards and crowd controllers need to get and renew a license?
description: Victoria Police security licensing: qualifications per activity, the 12 month rule, and first aid and refresher training for renewals from October 2026.
shortAnswer: In Victoria, private security work is licensed by the Victoria Police Licensing and Regulation Division under the Private Security Act 2004. Applicants must complete the approved qualification for each activity, such as CPP20218 Certificate II in Security Operations for unarmed guards and crowd controllers, with an approved RTO within 12 months of applying. From 5 October 2026, renewing individual operators must also complete HLTAID011 first aid and, for guards, crowd controllers and bodyguards, a Victoria Police approved refresher course.
keyTakeaways: Since 19 June 2025, under the Private Security and County Court Amendment Act 2024, every private security activity is a licensed activity; former registrations had to transition to licenses.

The seven licensed activities are investigator, bodyguard, crowd controller, security guard, private security trainer, security equipment installer and security adviser; security guards can hold up to six sub-activities.
Training must be with an approved Registered Training Organisation and must be valid within 12 months of the date the application is received.

From 5 October 2026, every individual operator renewing a license needs HLTAID011 Provide First Aid completed in the three years before expiry; bodyguards, crowd controllers and security guards also need the approved refresher course completed in the 12 months before renewal.
Clients who engage licensed security must complete a Risk Management Plan and give it to the licensee at least one day before the work, under sections 136A and 136B of the Act.
jurisdiction: Australia (Victoria): Private Security Act 2004, as amended by the Private Security and County Court Amendment Act 2024
regulator: Licensing and Regulation Division (LRD), Victoria Police
appliesTo: Security guards, including unarmed, armed, cash-in-transit, control room, monitoring center and dog handler sub-activities
Investigators, security equipment installers, security advisers and private security trainers
Independent contractors with an ABN for security work, who need both a business and an individual operator license
Clients that engage licensed security, who must prepare a Risk Management Plan

sections.heading: What changed in Victorian private security licensing in 2025 and 2026?

blocks.text: Victoria moved from a two tier system of licenses and registrations to licensing for every activity, then added training conditions for renewal. Victoria Police's [summary of the changes](https://www.police.vic.gov.au/changes-private-security-licences-and-registrations) says most provisions of the Private Security and County Court Amendment Act 2024 took effect on 19 June 2025, ending the old class A and class B activities and requiring registration holders to transition to a Private Security Individual Operator licence, a Private Security Business licence, or both.

items: 19 June 2025: all private security activities become licensed activities; suitability references and newspaper advertising of business applications are no longer required.

19 December 2025: independent contractors with an ABN related to their security activity must hold both a business license and an individual operator license (section 15A; private investigators are excluded).
5 October 2026: renewal of an individual operator license requires approved first aid training and, for some activities, the approved refresher course.

blocks.text: Because the renewal rules commenced only a month before this page was written, many licensees will meet them for the first time at their next renewal. Employers should check expiry dates now rather than wait for the renewal pack, which Victoria Police sends 10 weeks before a license expires.

sections.heading: Which qualification does each Victorian security activity require?

blocks.text: Each activity, and each security guard sub-activity, has its own approved qualification. Victoria Police's [eligibility and training page](https://www.police.vic.gov.au/private-security-eligibility-requirements-and-training) lists them and states that only training completed with an approved RTO is accepted, and that the training must be valid within 12 months of receipt of the application.

blocks.text: Applicants must also be 18 or over, have fingerprints taken, provide international police checks for any country lived in for more than 12 months in the previous 10 years since age 16, and not be a prohibited person under section 13 of the Act. Overseas students face an extra condition: Victoria Police will only recognize security courses that were delivered by an approved RTO and registered on CRICOS.

sections.heading: What training is needed to renew a Victorian security license?

blocks.text: From 5 October 2026, renewal depends on two pieces of training evidence. Victoria Police's [renewal page](https://www.police.vic.gov.au/renew-your-private-security-licence) says every individual operator must submit an HLTAID011 Provide First Aid certificate, and bodyguards, crowd controllers and security guards must also submit a certificate for the Victoria Police approved refresher training.

items: **First aid:** applies to bodyguards, crowd controllers, investigators, security advisers, security equipment installers, security guards and trainers. An existing HLTAID011 certificate can be used if it was completed in the three years before the license expires.

**Refresher course:** applies to bodyguards, crowd controllers and security guards. It must be completed in the 12 months before renewal, is available only online, and is hosted by the Australian Security Industry Association Limited (ASIAL).
**Exception:** holders whose only activity is security guard (monitoring centre operator) do not need the refresher but still need first aid.

blocks.title: Primary text: Victoria Police
blocks.text: "You must complete the refresher training course within the 12 months before your licence renewal."

The 12 month window is the part most likely to catch employers out. A refresher completed early, for example during a quiet season 14 months before expiry, will not count, so refresher scheduling should be driven by each person's expiry date rather than by a single annual training day.

sections.heading: What duties fall on clients and security businesses?

blocks.text: Clients now have a statutory role. Under sections 136A and 136B of the Private Security Act 2004, a client that employs or engages a security license holder must complete a Risk Management Plan before the activity is carried out and give a copy to the licensee at least one day beforehand. Victoria Police has published [templates](https://www.police.vic.gov.au/changes-private-security-licences-and-registrations) for unarmed crowd controller or security guard work and for unarmed bodyguard work.

Security businesses also face the section 15A rule: a subcontractor with an ABN related to the security activity must hold both a business license and an individual operator license, which is aimed at sham contracting. A provider's onboarding check should therefore confirm the license type as well as the endorsed activities.

sections.heading: How should a Victorian security provider evidence compliance?

blocks.text: A provider should be able to show, for each person and shift, the endorsed activity, the qualification behind it, and the renewal training that keeps it current. The table below is an illustrative template, not a Victoria Police form.

blocks.text: The same approach applies in New South Wales, where the license structure differs; compare [NSW security license training requirements](/regulations/nsw-security-licence-training-requirements). For scheduling rules that respect windows like the 12 month refresher, see [how to set mandatory training refresh cycles](/guides/how-to-set-mandatory-training-refresh-cycles), and for first aid across Australian workplaces generally, see [first aid training requirements in Australia](/regulations/first-aid-training-requirements-australia).

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry records the qualification, first aid and refresher as separate credentials with their own validity windows, and links each client's Risk Management Plan to the site briefing that operatives are assessed on. That lets a provider show both that a guard was licensed and that they were briefed on the specific risks identified for that job. See [audit evidence](/platform/audit-evidence).

faqs.q: Can someone who holds an interstate security license work in Victoria?
faqs.a: Not on the interstate license alone. They must apply for a Victorian license under mutual recognition, which is issued only for equivalent activities and not on interstate provisional licenses, or hold a Temporary Interstate Visitor Permit for a defined special event. Temporary permits cannot be renewed.

faqs.q: Do security equipment installers need training in Victoria?
faqs.a: Victoria Police states there are currently no training requirements for an individual license as a security equipment installer or security adviser. Since 19 June 2025 these are licensed activities, so probity, identity and fingerprinting requirements apply, and from 5 October 2026 first aid is required at renewal.

faqs.q: How old can a security qualification be when applying in Victoria?
faqs.a: Victoria Police requires training to be valid within 12 months of the date it receives the application. Someone who completed the Certificate II more than a year before applying should expect to retrain or seek advice from the Licensing and Regulation Division before lodging.

faqs.q: Who runs the Victorian security refresher course?
faqs.a: The refresher course is approved by Victoria Police, available only online, and hosted by the Australian Security Industry Association Limited (ASIAL). Licensees submit the completion certificate with their renewal application.

factCheck.claim: From 5 October 2026, renewing individual operators must complete HLTAID011 Provide First Aid (existing certificate accepted if completed in the three years before expiry) and bodyguards, crowd controllers and security guards must complete the approved refresher within 12 months before renewal; refresher online only, hosted by ASIAL; monitoring centre operator only holders exempt from refresher; renewal application sent 10 weeks before expiry; requirements follow amendments commencing 19 June 2025.

Most changes under the Private Security and County Court Amendment Act 2024 commenced 19 June 2025; all activities licensed; class A and B removed; seven activities defined; ABN contractors need both business and individual licences under section 15A from 19 December 2025 (not investigators); Risk Management Plans under sections 136A and 136B at least one day before the activity.

Training must be with an approved RTO and valid within 12 months of receipt of application; CPP20218 for crowd control, unarmed guard and control room operator; CPP31318 streams for armed guard, cash-in-transit and dog; CPP31418 for bodyguard; CPP30619 for investigator; CPP40719 or approved organisation membership for business licence; no training for installer or adviser; CRICOS condition for student visa holders; prohibited person defined in section 13.
A security guard may be licensed for up to six sub-activities; guard dogs must be trained to the obedience level defined by the Domestic Animals Regulations 2015.
Interstate licence holders apply under mutual recognition for equivalent activities only, not on provisional licences; temporary visitor permits for special events cannot be renewed.
